_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 4.5. No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

questions.scenario: How is 'mental disorder' defined for SOA 2003 offences?
options: Any disorder or disability of the mind (MHA 1983, s. 1)

questions.scenario: Under s. 30(2), B is 'unable to refuse' if…
options: B lacks the capacity to choose whether to agree, or is unable to communicate such a choice

questions.scenario: Under s. 30(2)(a), lack of capacity can arise from lack of understanding of the nature or consequences of the act or…
explanations: The Act says 'or for any other reason'.

questions.scenario: What did R v C (2009) decide about capacity?
options: Capacity is general – a person either has it or not
Capacity is specific to the person, the situation and the time; an irrational fear from the disorder can mean lack of capacity

questions.scenario: What must A know for ss. 30–33?
options: That B has a mental disorder and is likely to be unable to refuse – or A could reasonably be expected to know

questions.scenario: A has sex with B, who has a severe learning disability and can't understand what sex is. What is the maximum penalty (⚠)?
B has a learning disability but has capacity to choose. A offers B money to engage in sexual activity and B agrees. Which group of offences?
explanations: A is not a care worker.

questions.scenario: A care-home worker has a sexual relationship with a resident who has dementia, who appears to agree. Which is correct?
options: Care worker offence (s. 38) – consent and capacity are irrelevant

questions.scenario: Which is an exception to the care worker offences?
options: A and B were married/civil partners, or had a lawful sexual relationship before the care relationship began

questions.scenario: For care worker offences, what kind of contact must A have with B?
options: Regular face-to-face contact in the course of providing care

questions.scenario: A causes B, who lacks capacity due to mental disorder, to watch a sexual act for A's gratification. Which section?
B has autism and is physically able but cannot communicate her choice to A due to her disorder. Which applies?
options: s. 30(2)(b) – unable to communicate a choice

questions.scenario: A tells B, who has a mental disorder, that the police will take her away unless she has sex with him. Which section?
Who decides whether B had capacity in a trial?
options: The jury, on the evidence (often including expert evidence)

questions.scenario: A lies to B, who has a learning disability, that he is a doctor and the sexual touching is a medical test. Which group could apply?
explanations: Correct (s. 76 may also apply to s. 3 ⚠).

questions.scenario: Can a person with a mental disorder consent to sexual activity?
options: Yes, if they have capacity to choose and are not induced/threatened/deceived

questions.scenario: What is the maximum for non-penetrative s. 30 sexual activity (⚠)?
A takes advantage of B, whose irrational fear (caused by her schizophrenia) stops her refusing. Under R v C…
options: She had capacity because she understood sex
She may lack capacity to choose – the fear prevents her exercising choice
questions.manualRef: Blackstone's 2027 · 4.5 · R v C – irrational fear

questions.scenario: Which group requires that B DOES have capacity?
explanations: Correct (B agrees because of inducement etc.).

questions.scenario: A care worker (ss. 38–41) must know or could reasonably be expected to know…
options: That B has a mental disorder
